title: Sweep model depth (DEPTH=8 → 10)
justification: At fixed training FLOPs/time budget, small transformers are typically more sample-efficient per-token when made modestly deeper rather than wider, and depth is completely unexplored in the log so far.
detail:
Single-line change: set `DEPTH = 10` (from 8) in the hyperparameters block, leaving `ASPECT_RATIO=64` and `HEAD_DIM=128` unchanged. This raises base_dim to 640, which rounds up to model_dim=640 (5 heads at head_dim=128) via `build_model_config`. Everything else (batch size, LRs, schedules, window pattern) stays as-is since `setup_optimizer`'s `dmodel_lr_scale` already adjusts AdamW LRs for the new model_dim automatically. This isolates the depth/width tradeoff as the only variable. If this improves val_bpb, a natural follow-up is a small grid around depth (e.g. 9, 11) to find the local optimum; if it regresses, it suggests the original DEPTH=8 choice was already near-optimal for this 5-min budget and the log should note not to repeat depth sweeps.</detail>
<parameter name="notes">Given this script is already heavily tuned (Muon+NorMuon, value embeddings, sliding window pattern, polar-express orthogonalization) it looks like it derives from a well-optimized nanochat/modded-nanogpt lineage — architecture-level micro-tweaks may have already been tried by the original author before this cell started, so depth is one of the few large untested levers left.

title: Extend depth sweep: DEPTH=10 → 12
justification: Depth 8→10 gave a clear, consistent win (~1.2% bpb reduction across 5 seeds), so the depth-vs-width tradeoff curve for this time budget likely hasn't peaked yet at 10.
detail:
Set `DEPTH = 12` (from 10) in the hyperparameters block; base_dim becomes 768, rounding to model_dim=768 (6 heads at head_dim=128) via `build_model_config`. Everything else (ASPECT_RATIO=64, HEAD_DIM=128, batch size, LR schedule) stays unchanged since `dmodel_lr_scale` auto-adjusts AdamW LRs. Watch peak VRAM (was 66.5GB at depth=10) — if it's near the GPU limit, drop `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE` from 128 to 96 or 64 (compensating with more grad_accum_steps so TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE stays fixed) to keep memory headroom.</detail>

title: Extend depth sweep: DEPTH=10 -> 12
description: Set DEPTH=12 (model_dim 640->768, 6 heads); also reduced DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->64 (more grad_accum_steps) to stay within VRAM headroom.
reflection: val_bpb regressed to 1.016037, worse than depth=10's 1.002279 and even worse than the original depth=8 baseline of 1.014027. This shows depth=10 was at or past the local optimum for this 5-minute time budget -- further depth increase is a net loss, likely because the smaller device batch size (needed to fit VRAM) and/or larger model reduces effective tokens-per-second and steps taken in the fixed wall-clock budget. Recommend not pushing depth further; a finer probe at DEPTH=11 (with device batch size kept at 128 if it fits) might be worth one more small experiment, but expect diminishing or negative returns. VRAM at depth=12/batch=64 was only 48990MB, well under the depth=10/batch=128 66.5GB, suggesting batch size reduction was overly conservative and may have hurt throughput -- a future depth=11 test should try to keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 if it fits to avoid confounding the depth change with a batch-size change.

title: Extend depth sweep: DEPTH=10 -> 12

reflection: Regressed sharply: val_bpb 1.016254, worse than both the depth=10 baseline (1.002279) and the original depth=8 baseline (1.014027). Peak VRAM was only 49.0GB, well under budget, meaning the DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE cut to 64 was unnecessary caution and likely hurt via lower MFU (smaller batches -> more kernel-launch/overhead per token, fewer effective tokens processed in the fixed 300s wall-clock budget) on top of depth=12 having more FLOPs/token. Recommend: do NOT extend depth further without keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 (VRAM clearly wasn't the constraint), and treat depth=10 as the local optimum for this time budget unless someone reruns depth=12 at batch=128 to isolate the two effects.

justification: Muon drives updates for the vast majority of parameters (all transformer matrices) and its LR has never been touched in this log — two rounds of depth sweeps found a local optimum on architecture, but optimizer LR is a completely untested, potentially higher-leverage lever.
detail:
Starting from current baseline (DEPTH=10, all else unchanged), change only `MATRIX_LR = 0.04` to `MATRIX_LR = 0.05` (a 25% increase). Everything else (ASPECT_RATIO, HEAD_DIM, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128, EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, SCALAR_LR, WEIGHT_DECAY, schedules) stays fixed so the LR change is isolated. This directly scales the `lr` passed into Muon param groups in `setup_optimizer`, which flows into `muon_step_fused` via `group["lr"] * max(1.0, shape[-2]/shape[-1])**0.5`. If 0.05 improves val_bpb, a natural follow-up is 0.06 or a symmetric check at 0.03 to map the curve; if it regresses, try 0.03 instead (lower LR) since we won't know a priori which direction is better without a first data point.</detail>

title: Lower weight decay for short training budget (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 → 0.1)
justification: Four rounds of LR-magnitude/schedule sweeps near DEPTH=10 all failed; weight decay is untested, and strong decay (0.2) may over-shrink weights in this short, few-thousand-step regime.
detail: In the hyperparameters block, change `WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2` to `WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1` (from current DEPTH=10 baseline, everything else unchanged: ASPECT_RATIO=64, HEAD_DIM=128, MATRIX_LR=0.04, WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128). This flows into `setup_optimizer`'s Muon param groups (`weight_decay=weight_decay`) and then `get_weight_decay(progress) = WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress)`, which is applied each step in `muon_step_fused` as cautious decay (`lr * wd * stacked_params * mask`). Halving the base value halves the decay pressure throughout training while preserving the same linear anneal-to-zero shape. If this improves val_bpb, a natural follow-up is WEIGHT_DECAY=0.05 or 0.0 (no decay); if it regresses, the untested direction (raising to 0.3) becomes the next candidate.
notes: This is a genuinely new axis (optimizer regularization strength) rather than another increment on LR magnitude/schedule, which is the region that's produced 4 consecutive misses. If other agents also propose WEIGHT_DECAY changes, I'd defer to whichever direction has the stronger mechanistic argument, but I'd resist re-proposing yet another MATRIX_LR or WARMDOWN_RATIO variant since that space looks saturated.

title: Lower weight decay (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.1)
description: Halved cautious Muon weight decay from 0.2 to 0.1, all else unchanged from DEPTH=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 1.003940 vs baseline 1.002279 - a small regression, not an improvement. This is the fifth consecutive round where a single-axis hyperparameter perturbation (depth up, matrix_lr up, matrix_lr down, warmdown up, now weight_decay down) has failed to beat the DEPTH=10 baseline, suggesting the baseline sits in a fairly flat, well-tuned local optimum across these axes. Future rounds should probably stop doing isolated 1D sweeps of already-tuned scalars and instead try a genuinely different lever (e.g. window_pattern, MLP expansion ratio, aspect_ratio independent of depth, or combining two previously-near-neutral changes) rather than another single-knob nudge.

title: Lower weight decay (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.1)
description: Halved cautious Muon weight decay from 0.2 to 0.1, everything else unchanged from DEPTH=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 1.003675, worse than baseline 1.002279 (about +0.14%). This is the fifth consecutive round where a single isolated hyperparameter perturbation near the current baseline has failed to improve on it -- depth up, matrix_lr up, matrix_lr down, warmdown ratio up, and now weight_decay down have all regressed by similar small margins (~0.3-0.4%). The baseline set at DEPTH=10 appears to be at or very near a fairly sharp local optimum across multiple independent axes (architecture, Muon LR magnitude in both directions, LR schedule shape, and now regularization strength). Future rounds should stop doing single-axis +/-25% perturbations around this point and instead try either (a) a qualitatively different mechanism (e.g. architecture: window pattern, MLP width ratio, value-embedding gating) or (b) a joint/correlated change, since independent axes have each been probed and each one taken alone loses.

title: Lower weight decay for short training budget
description: Changed WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 (halved cautious Muon weight decay), all else unchanged from DEPTH=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 1.003733, worse than baseline 1.002279 — another miss. Five rounds of single-axis perturbations around the DEPTH=10 baseline (depth up, matrix_lr up, matrix_lr down, warmdown ratio up, weight_decay down) have now all failed to beat it, each landing in a similar 1.0037-1.006 band regardless of direction. This is a strong signal that DEPTH=10 with the original LR/WD/schedule values is a genuinely tight local optimum for isolated hyperparameter nudges, and further single-knob sweeps in this neighborhood are unlikely to pay off. Future rounds should consider either a qualitatively different axis (e.g. window pattern, MLP width ratio, batch size/grad-accum tradeoff, embedding LR) or a combination of two previously-tested directions rather than another isolated increment.

title: Lower weight decay for short training budget (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.1)
description: Halved WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 (cautious Muon decay), all else unchanged from DEPTH=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 1.004031, worse than baseline 1.002279. Halving weight decay regressed, roughly in line with the magnitude of regression seen from MATRIX_LR up/down sweeps and WARMDOWN_RATIO changes (~1.002 -> ~1.005-1.006). This is now the fifth consecutive round where a single-axis perturbation from the DEPTH=10 baseline (depth, matrix_lr up, matrix_lr down, warmdown ratio, weight decay) has failed to beat it. Strong signal that this baseline sits in a fairly tight, well-tuned local optimum across many of the obvious single-hyperparameter axes. Future rounds should consider: (a) axes not yet touched at all (EMBEDDING_LR, ADAM_BETAS, WINDOW_PATTERN, ASPECT_RATIO independent of depth, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE/grad_accum tradeoffs), or (b) treating this as evidence the baseline is close to optimal for isolated single-parameter changes and that further gains may require joint/correlated changes rather than one-at-a-time sweeps.

title: Lower weight decay for short training budget (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.1)
description: Halved WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1, all else unchanged from DEPTH=10 baseline.
reflection: val_bpb 1.003496, slightly worse than baseline 1.002279. Weight decay is not the lever: neither this halving nor (implicitly) the current 0.2 default seem to be the bottleneck. Five rounds now (depth up/down, matrix_lr up/down, warmdown length, weight decay down) have all failed to beat the DEPTH=10 baseline, suggesting the current hyperparameter configuration sits in a fairly robust local optimum for single-axis perturbations. Future rounds should consider a genuinely different lever (e.g. architecture changes like window pattern, MLP ratio, or embedding LR) rather than another one-off LR/regularization tweak, or accept that this baseline may be close to the practical ceiling for this time budget.
